module_title: Burgers and Sandwiches on the Go

lessons.title: Crafting the Perfect Burger Patty
lessons.body: Start with the right meat. In Africa, beef is common, but you can also use goat, lamb, or even camel. For a juicy patty, use meat with 20% fat. If your butcher only has lean meat, ask for extra fat or mix in 10% beef suet. Grind the meat yourself if possible, using a 5mm plate. If you buy pre-ground, use it within 24 hours. For 10 patties of 150g each, you need 1.5kg meat. Add 1 teaspoon salt per 500g meat, 1 teaspoon black pepper, and 1 chopped onion (optional). Do not overmix; just combine. Shape into balls, then flatten to 1.5cm thick and 10cm wide. Make a small indentation in the center with your thumb to prevent puffing. Chill for 30 minutes before cooking. Cook on a hot cast-iron pan or grill at medium-high heat (200Â°C). For medium doneness, cook 3 minutes per side, flipping once. Use a meat thermometer: 71Â°C for well done. If you don't have one, cut a patty open; juices should run clear. For high volume, cook on a flat-top griddle. Clean your griddle between batches. In Africa, charcoal grills are common; use them for smoky flavor. But for takeaway, a flat-top gives consistent results. Always rest patties for 2 minutes before assembling. This keeps them juicy. If you want a crispy edge, press down lightly with a spatula for 10 seconds after flipping. Never press while cooking; it squeezes out juices. For a healthier option, mix in 20% finely chopped mushrooms or lentils. But for classic taste, stick to beef. Remember, food safety: keep raw meat below 5Â°C and cook to 71Â°C. Wash hands and surfaces with soap after handling raw meat.

lessons.title: Buns and Breads: Brioche, Potato, and Ciabatta
lessons.body: The bun is as important as the patty. For takeaway, you need buns that hold up to sauces and wrapping. Brioche is soft, slightly sweet, and rich. Recipe for 12 buns: 500g strong white flour, 10g salt, 50g sugar, 10g instant yeast, 200ml warm milk, 4 eggs, 250g soft butter. Mix flour, salt, sugar, yeast. Add milk and eggs, knead 10 minutes. Add butter a little at a time, knead until smooth. Rise 1 hour. Divide into 80g balls, shape, place on tray, rise 30 minutes. Egg wash, bake at 180Â°C for 15-20 minutes. Potato buns are softer and stay moist longer. Replace 100g flour with 100g mashed potato, reduce milk to 150ml. Ciabatta is crusty and chewy, good for sandwiches. Use 500g flour, 10g salt, 5g yeast, 400ml water. Mix, rest 30 minutes, fold, rest 30 minutes, fold again. Rise 1 hour. Shape into flat loaves, bake at 220Â°C with steam for 25 minutes. For Africa, you can use local flours like cassava or millet blended with wheat. But start with wheat for consistency. If you don't have an oven, you can steam buns: shape, place on greased tray, steam for 15 minutes, then finish on a dry pan. For high volume, make dough ahead, refrigerate overnight for slow rise. That improves flavor. Always slice buns horizontally, toast cut sides on a hot pan for 30 seconds. This prevents sogginess. Store baked buns in airtight bags at room temperature for 2 days, or freeze for 1 month. For takeaway, choose buns that are slightly dense so they don't fall apart. Brioche is great for premium burgers, potato for everyday, ciabatta for rustic sandwiches.

lessons.title: Condiments and Sauces: Aioli, Relish, and Special Sauce
lessons.body: Sauces make your burger memorable. Start with aioli: 2 egg yolks, 2 garlic cloves (crushed), 1 teaspoon salt, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 250ml neutral oil (sunflower). Whisk yolks, garlic, salt, lemon. Slowly add oil drop by drop while whisking, then in a thin stream until thick. If it breaks, start with a new yolk and whisk in the broken mixture. For a African twist, add 1 teaspoon harissa or peri-peri sauce. Relish: 2 cups chopped tomatoes, 1 chopped onion, 1 chopped bell pepper, 1 cup vinegar, 1/2 cup sugar, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon mustard seeds. Simmer 30 minutes until thick. Cool and jar. Special sauce: 1 cup mayonnaise, 1/4 cup ketchup, 2 tablespoons pickle relish, 1 tablespoon mustard, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder. Mix well. For takeaway, sauces must be thick so they don't drip. Add a little cornstarch slurry (1 teaspoon cornstarch + 1 tablespoon water) to relish while cooking. For aioli, use pasteurized eggs if you're worried about salmonella. In Africa, you can use local oils like groundnut oil. Store sauces in squeeze bottles for speed. Label with dates; use within 5 days refrigerated. For high volume, make in large batches: 5 litres at a time. Use a stick blender for aioli. For relish, a large pot. Always taste and adjust salt, sugar, acid. For vegan options, use vegan mayonnaise (soy or aquafaba based). Aioli can be made with aquafaba: 3 tablespoons aquafaba, 1 teaspoon mustard, 1 tablespoon lemon, 250ml oil, whisk until thick. For a smoky sauce, add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika. For heat, add chopped chilli. Keep sauces cold during service. Use an ice bath under squeeze bottles. Never leave sauces at room temperature for more than 2 hours. For takeaway, pack sauces in small sealed cups or apply directly to burger before wrapping. If applying directly, use 1-2 tablespoons per burger.

lessons.title: Assembly and Wrapping Techniques for Take Away
lessons.body: Assembly line is key for speed. Set up: toasted buns, cooked patties (held at 60Â°C), cheese slices, sauces in squeeze bottles, lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles. For one burger: bottom bun, 1 tablespoon special sauce, 1 lettuce leaf, 1 tomato slice, 1 patty, 1 cheese slice (if using), 1 tablespoon relish, 3 pickle slices, top bun. Press gently. For takeaway, wrap tightly. Use foil-lined paper or wax paper. Cut a square 30cm x 30cm. Place burger in center. Fold bottom corner up over burger, then fold left and right corners in, then roll to top. Tuck ends. Or use a burger clamshell box: place burger, close lid. For high volume, pre-wrap in foil and keep in a warm box at 60Â°C. Do not stack more than 3 high. For sandwiches, use a similar method. For a chicken sandwich, use a 150g fillet, cook 4 minutes per side. Assemble: bottom bun, mayo, lettuce, tomato, fillet, top bun. Wrap in paper. For a vegan burger, use a bean patty: 400g cooked black beans, 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon paprika, 50g breadcrumbs. Mash, shape, cook 3 minutes per side. Assemble same way. For wrapping, you can also use banana leaves for a local touch. Steam banana leaf for 30 seconds to make pliable. Wrap burger, secure with string. This keeps it warm and adds aroma. For takeaway, always include a napkin and a small packet of sauce if not applied. Label with order number. Keep hot food above 60Â°C and cold below 5Â°C. Use insulated bags for delivery. Train staff to wrap in under 30 seconds. Practice with a timer. For large orders, assign one person to assembly, one to wrapping, one to bagging. This reduces errors.

lessons.title: Vegan and Vegetarian Burger Options
lessons.body: Vegan and vegetarian burgers are growing in demand. For a basic bean burger: 2 cans (800g) black beans, drained and rinsed. Mash with a fork. Add 1 chopped onion, 2 garlic cloves (minced), 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon salt, 100g breadcrumbs, 2 tablespoons flaxseed mixed with 6 tablespoons water (flax egg). Mix well. Shape into 6 patties. Chill 30 minutes. Cook on a hot pan with 1 tablespoon oil, 4 minutes per side. For a lentil burger: 200g cooked green lentils, 100g cooked quinoa, 1 grated carrot, 1 teaspoon curry powder, 50g oats, 2 tablespoons tomato paste. Mix, shape, cook. For a mushroom burger: 400g finely chopped mushrooms, 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 100g breadcrumbs, 2 tablespoons soy sauce. SautÃ© mushrooms until dry, mix, shape, cook. For a vegetarian (not vegan) option, add 1 egg and 50g grated cheese. For a vegan cheese slice, use cashew cheese: 100g cashews soaked 4 hours, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 tablespoon nutritional yeast, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 100ml water. Blend until smooth, spread in a tray, set in fridge. For a crispy coating, dip patties in flour, then plant milk, then breadcrumbs. Fry at 180Â°C for 3 minutes per side. For Africa, use local ingredients: black-eyed peas, cassava, plantain. Plantain burger: 2 ripe plantains, mashed, 100g breadcrumbs, 1 teaspoon ginger, 1 teaspoon chilli. Shape, fry. Always offer vegan buns: most buns contain milk and eggs, so use a simple water-based bun: 500g flour, 10g salt, 7g yeast, 300ml water, 2 tablespoons oil. Mix, knead, rise, shape, bake. For sauces, use vegan mayo, ketchup, mustard, relish. For takeaway, wrap separately to avoid cross-contamination. Use separate tongs. Label clearly. Cook vegan patties on a separate pan or clean griddle. For high volume, make patties ahead, freeze. Cook from frozen at 180Â°C for 5 minutes per side. Test one to ensure hot throughout (74Â°C).

lessons.title: Cooking Burgers in High Volume
lessons.body: High volume means serving 100+ burgers per hour. You need a flat-top griddle at least 1 meter wide, or multiple charcoal grills. For gas griddle, preheat to 200Â°C. For charcoal, light charcoal 30 minutes before. Use a temperature gun to check. Organize your station: raw patties on left, cooked on right, buns in center, sauces and toppings in front. Use a timer. For beef patties, cook from fresh or thawed. If frozen, thaw in fridge overnight. Never thaw at room temperature. For 100 patties, you need 15kg beef. Shape into 150g balls, then press on griddle with a burger press. Cook 3 minutes, flip, add cheese, cook 2 minutes. For medium, internal temp 71Â°C. Use a probe thermometer. For speed, cook in batches of 20. Keep cooked patties in a warming tray at 60Â°C. Do not hold more than 20 minutes. For buns, toast on griddle for 30 seconds. For assembly, use an assembly line: one person sauces buns, one adds lettuce, one adds patty, one wraps. For wrapping, use foil. For large orders, use a conveyor belt toaster if available. For charcoal grills, you can cook 20 patties at a time. Use a chimney starter. Keep charcoal topped up. For a smoky flavor, add soaked wood chips. For vegan patties, cook on a separate griddle to avoid cross-contamination. For high volume, pre-portion sauces in squeeze bottles. Use a scale for consistent patty size. Train staff on food safety: wash hands every 30 minutes, change gloves. Keep raw and cooked separate. Use color-coded cutting boards. For delivery, use insulated bags. For orders of 10+ burgers, offer a discount. Track your times: from order to bag should be under 5 minutes. Use a POS system or a simple notebook. For cost control, calculate cost per burger: beef 150g = $1.50, bun = $0.30, sauce = $0.10, packaging = $0.20. Total $2.10. Sell at $5. Profit $2.90. For 100 burgers, profit $290. Reinvest in equipment. Keep a clean station. At the end of day, clean griddle with scraper and oil. Store leftovers properly.

quiz.q: What percentage of fat is ideal for a juicy burger patty?
quiz.explanation: 20% fat ensures juiciness and flavor without being too greasy.

quiz.q: What is the internal temperature for a well-done beef burger?
quiz.explanation: 71Â°C is the safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef.

quiz.q: Why make an indentation in the center of a burger patty?
quiz.explanation: The indentation prevents the patty from swelling into a dome shape during cooking.

quiz.q: How long should you rest a cooked patty before assembling?
quiz.explanation: Resting for 2 minutes allows juices to redistribute, keeping the patty moist.

quiz.q: Which bun is described as soft, slightly sweet, and rich?
quiz.explanation: Brioche contains butter and eggs, giving it a rich, sweet flavor and soft texture.

quiz.q: What is a key ingredient in potato buns that keeps them moist?
quiz.explanation: Mashed potato adds moisture and softness to the bun.

quiz.q: How long should you steam buns if you don't have an oven?
quiz.explanation: Steaming for 15 minutes cooks the buns through, then they can be finished on a pan.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of toasting cut sides of buns?
quiz.explanation: Toasting creates a barrier that stops sauces from making the bun soggy.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of aioli breaking?
quiz.explanation: Adding oil too fast prevents proper emulsification, causing the sauce to separate.

quiz.q: Which ingredient can be used as a vegan substitute for egg yolks in aioli?
quiz.explanation: Aquafaba (chickpea water) whips up like egg whites and can emulsify oil.

quiz.q: What is a key step to make relish thick for takeaway?
quiz.explanation: Cornstarch slurry thickens the relish so it doesn't drip.

quiz.q: How long can you store homemade sauces in the refrigerator?
quiz.explanation: Most homemade sauces keep for up to 5 days when refrigerated.

quiz.q: What is a good way to keep sauces cold during service?
quiz.explanation: An ice bath under squeeze bottles keeps sauces at a safe cold temperature.

quiz.q: In assembling a burger, what goes directly on the bottom bun?
quiz.explanation: Sauce on the bottom bun adds flavor and acts as a moisture barrier.

quiz.q: What is the recommended internal holding temperature for cooked patties?
quiz.explanation: 60Â°C is the minimum safe holding temperature for hot foods.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of wrapping burgers in banana leaves?
quiz.explanation: Banana leaves impart a subtle aroma and keep the burger warm.

quiz.q: How can you prevent cross-contamination when cooking vegan patties?
quiz.explanation: Separate cooking surfaces prevent meat juices from contacting vegan food.

quiz.q: What is a common binder in vegan burger patties?
quiz.explanation: Flaxseed mixed with water forms a gel that binds ingredients together.

quiz.q: Which of these is a typical ingredient in a bean burger?
quiz.explanation: Black beans are a common base for vegetarian burgers.

quiz.q: What temperature should you cook vegan patties to for safety?
quiz.explanation: 74Â°C ensures any potential bacteria are killed, especially if using eggs or dairy.

quiz.q: What is a key equipment for high-volume burger cooking?
quiz.explanation: A flat-top griddle allows cooking many patties at once and is easy to clean.

quiz.q: How many patties can you cook at once on a 1-meter griddle?
quiz.explanation: A 1-meter griddle can hold about 20 patties (each 10cm wide) with space for flipping.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid pressing down on a burger while cooking?
quiz.explanation: Pressing forces out flavorful juices, resulting in a dry patty.

quiz.q: What is the maximum time you should hold cooked patties in a warming tray?
quiz.explanation: Holding longer than 20 minutes can dry out patties and increase food safety risk.

quiz.q: What is a good way to ensure consistent patty size?
quiz.explanation: Using a scale ensures each patty weighs the same, cooking evenly.

quiz.q: What is the target time from order to bag for high-volume service?
quiz.explanation: Under 5 minutes keeps customers happy and food hot.

quiz.q: What is a key food safety practice for high-volume cooking?
options: B) Use same gloves all day
C) Store raw and cooked together
quiz.explanation: Frequent handwashing prevents cross-contamination.

quiz.q: What is a good African twist for aioli?
quiz.explanation: Harissa or peri-peri adds a spicy North African flavor.

quiz.q: What is a typical ingredient in a plantain burger?
quiz.explanation: Mashed ripe plantains form the base of this sweet and savory patty.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a flax egg in vegan burgers?
quiz.explanation: Flax egg acts as a binder, replacing the need for chicken eggs.
